letters.Timeline A: Dear you, as you consider whether to quit your corporate job and start your own company, remember that stability and security can be a powerful foundation for happiness. At 35, you have the opportunity to build a life that is rooted in community and relationships. By Year 10, you'll have an income of 64 LPA, happiness of 90, and stress levels of 50. You'll look back on the decision to stay in your corporate job and build a fulfilling life around it with a sense of pride and contentment. One thing that was harder than expected was finding the right balance between work and personal life, but you'll learn to prioritize your relationships and health. My advice to you is to focus on building strong relationships and a sense of community, as these will be the foundation of your happiness and fulfillment.
letters.Timeline B: Dear you, as you consider whether to quit your corporate job and start your own company, remember that strategic ambition and calculated risk-taking can lead to great rewards. By Year 10, you'll have an income of 90 LPA, happiness of 95, and stress levels of 70. You'll look back on the decision to start your own company with a sense of pride and accomplishment. One thing that was harder than expected was navigating the challenges of entrepreneurship, but you'll learn to be resilient and adaptable. My advice to you is to stay focused on your goals and be willing to take calculated risks to achieve them.
letters.Timeline C: Dear you, as you consider whether to quit your corporate job and start your own company, remember that the high-risk, high-reward path can come with significant personal costs. By Year 10, you'll have an income of 100 LPA, happiness of 100, and stress levels of 95. You'll look back on the decision to start your own company with a sense of pride and accomplishment, but also with a sense of regret and loss. One thing that was harder than expected was the toll that the constant stress and pressure took on your relationships and health. My advice to you is to be aware of the potential costs of your decisions and to prioritize your well-being and relationships, even in the pursuit of greatness.

comparison.common_patterns: all three timelines show an increase in income and happiness over time, with a corresponding increase in stress levels, highlighting the trade-offs between financial success, personal fulfillment, and well-being
comparison.key_differences: the biggest divergence is between Timeline A and Timeline C, with Timeline A prioritizing stability and relationships, and Timeline C prioritizing opportunity and career growth, leading to significantly different outcomes in terms of stress levels, relationships, and overall well-being, particularly noticeable by Year 5
comparison.hinge_point: the single year and node where the three paths diverge most sharply is Year 1, with the decision to quit or stay in the corporate job, which sets the tone for the rest of the timeline and has a significant impact on the subsequent years, particularly in terms of career growth, stress levels, and relationships
